Project Brief: Win Back the Customer
IT2226 AI Innovation and Deep Learning Project  |  Team project (4 students)  |  Duration: 17 weeks
1. About this project
Your team will act as an AI solutions team engaged by an online retailer. You will study the business situation, explore and prepare the company's data, and design, build and evaluate an AI solution that helps the company's staff make better decisions.
The project assesses your ability to apply two areas of AI together:
Supervised deep learning: training, evaluating and justifying a deep learning model on the data provided.
Agentic AI: building an AI agent that reasons, uses tools (including your trained model) and takes actions to help staff solve real business problems.
This brief describes the client, its current situation, the problem, and what its staff wish for. It deliberately does not tell you how to solve the problem. Choosing an approach and justifying it is part of what you are assessed on.
Item
Details
Team size
4 students
Duration
16 weeks
Client (fictional)
ShopSphere Global, an online retailer
Data
ShopSphere data pack: 17 data tables and 4 policy documents (see section 7)
2. Client background
ShopSphere Global (a fictional company created for this project) is an online retailer founded in 2022. It sells about 400 products in eight categories (Electronics, Fashion, Home & Living, Beauty, Sports & Outdoors, Toys & Kids, Groceries, and Books & Media) to customers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and India, through its website and mobile app.
The company has grown quickly. Revenue is strongly seasonal: November (Singles' Day and Black Friday) and December are its busiest months. Its customers belong to a four-tier loyalty programme, ShopSphere Rewards (Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum).
3. The current situation
ShopSphere's leadership team is worried. The business keeps signing up new customers, but about one in three customers who have signed up have not visited the site at all in the last 90 days. Marketing spend keeps rising, while nobody can say with confidence which spending is working. The teaching team interviewed staff across the company, and their comments are summarised below.
3.1 CRM and Retention team
Every Monday, two CRM executives build the week's "win-back" list. They export data from the customer database, the order system, the preference centre and the helpdesk into spreadsheets, match them by hand, and choose customers mainly by how long it has been since their last order. Most customers on the list receive the same 10% voucher. Building the list takes about a day and a half.
What staff say
"By the time the list is ready, it's already out of date. And we keep giving vouchers to people who would have bought anyway." (CRM Manager)
"Last quarter we sent a 20% voucher to Bronze customers by mistake. The policy says Platinum only. Nobody noticed for weeks." (CRM Executive)
3.2 Marketing
Marketing runs Email, Search, Display, Social and Affiliate campaigns, each targeted at a region. Results are reported in a monthly slide deck put together from the marketing platform's exports. The team cannot easily compare channels, regions or seasons.
What staff say
"I need to see, at a glance, what's trending and which campaigns pay back. Right now I find out a month later." (Head of Marketing)
3.3 Customer Service
About 30 agents handle email, live chat, phone and WhatsApp tickets. Volumes roughly double in November and December. To reply properly, agents have to look up the customer's orders, deliveries and earlier tickets in three different systems.
What staff say
"A customer whose parcel was lost got a 'We miss you, here's 10% off' email the same day they complained. That's how we lose people." (Customer Service Lead)
3.4 Operations
ShopSphere ships through seven carriers. Late deliveries are tracked, but the information isn't linked to customer behaviour.
What staff say
"I suspect some carriers are costing us customers, not just money. I can't prove it." (Operations Manager)
3.5 Merchandising and Finance
What staff say
"Marketing promoted a product we had zero stock of, and discounted items with margins too thin to discount." (Merchandising Lead)
"Each country gets a weekly retention budget. I want to know before the money is spent that it's going to the right customers, and afterwards whether it worked." (Finance Controller)
4. Problem statement
Problem statement
ShopSphere's staff make important weekly decisions (who to re-engage, how, with which offer and through which channel) without knowing which customers are likely to purchase soon and which are drifting away. The information they need is spread across separate systems and policy documents, and pulling it together by hand is slow, inconsistent and error-prone. Managers also lack a timely view of the trends that would tell them whether these decisions are working.
How might ShopSphere use its customer, behavioural and operational data, together with AI, to predict which customers will make a purchase in the next 30 days, and help its staff turn that prediction into timely, consistent, policy-compliant and cost-effective decisions?
5. Stakeholder wish list
The wish list below comes from ShopSphere's stakeholders. It is a list of needs, not a specification. You must explain which items you chose to address, which you did not, and why.
#
Wish
Raised by
W1
Know which customers are likely to make a purchase in the next 30 days.
CRM Manager
W2
Understand why a customer is likely or unlikely to purchase, in terms staff can act on.
CRM Manager, Country Managers
W3
Each week, get a recommended re-engagement list (who to contact, which offer, which channel) that stays within each country's budget.
CRM Manager, Finance Controller
W4
Be certain every recommendation follows company policy: consent, contact frequency, open complaints, tier eligibility, stock and margin.
CRM Manager, Customer Service Lead
W5
Before replying, give a customer service agent a one-screen summary of the customer: orders, deliveries, earlier tickets and any recent offers.
Customer Service Lead
W6
A dashboard showing trends in sales, traffic, campaign performance, delivery performance and customer activity, by country and over time.
Head of Marketing, Operations Manager, Leadership
W7
Ask business questions in plain language and get one answer that pulls together information from several sources.
Leadership, Finance Controller
W8
Draft personalised messages in the customer's preferred language and channel.
CRM Executive
W9
Keep humans in control: nothing is sent without approval, and every decision has a recorded reason.
CRM Manager
W10
After a campaign, find out whether the money spent made a difference.
Finance Controller
6. Project requirements
Whatever approach you choose, your solution must:
1. include a supervised deep learning model trained on the data pack to predict the target in train.csv, evaluated properly and compared fairly against at least one non-deep-learning baseline;
2. include an agentic AI component that uses your trained model as part of its reasoning or actions;
3. address at least five wish-list items, including W1, W3 and W6;
4. use information from at least four different tables or documents in the data pack when making a decision;
5. be demonstrated as a working prototype that ShopSphere staff could realistically use;
6. be evaluated with evidence: both the model and the agent;
7. consider responsible AI: fairness, privacy and consent, transparency, and the risk of the system being wrong.
7. The data pack
The data pack is ShopSphere's data extract as at 30 September 2024. The target in train.csv shows whether each customer made at least one purchase between 1 and 30 October 2024. All the data is synthetic and contains no real personal information.
The core tables follow the structure of the Kaggle competition Global E-Commerce Customer Purchase Prediction. They have been regenerated and extended by the NYP teaching team to reflect ShopSphere's operations. The full data dictionary is in Appendix A and in DATA_README.md in the data pack.
Group
Files
What they describe
Customer
customers.csv, customer_preferences.csv, geo_data.csv
Profiles, loyalty tier, consent and contact preferences, regional socio-economic data
Behaviour
sessions.csv, transactions.csv, transaction_items.csv
Browsing sessions, orders and order lines, January 2022 to September 2024
Marketing
marketing_campaigns.csv, campaign_daily_performance.csv, retention_contact_history.csv
Campaigns (completed, active and planned), daily spend and results, retention offers sent
Operations
products.csv, deliveries.csv, support_tickets.csv
Catalogue, stock and margin; shipments and delays; customer service tickets with customers' messages
Finance and CRM
offer_catalogue.csv, retention_budget_2024Q4.csv
Allowed retention offers; weekly budget per country for Q4 2024
Labels
train.csv, test.csv, sample_submission.csv
64,000 labelled customers; 16,000 customers to predict
Policies
retention_offer_policy.md, shipping_and_returns_policy.md, customer_service_sla.md, loyalty_programme.md
ShopSphere's business rules
Watch out: The data is messy
Like real company data, the pack contains inconsistent spellings, several encodings for true/false, numbers stored as text, missing values, outliers and duplicates. Some tables were exported by different systems. Treat data preparation as a real part of the project, and check the data itself rather than relying only on the documentation.
You may create additional synthetic data if your solution needs it. Any data you create must be documented and clearly labelled as synthetic. The data pack itself must not be altered.
8. Deliverables and milestones
Week
Deliverable
What it must contain
3
Project proposal (max 6 pages) and 10-minute pitch
Stakeholders and their needs; the wish-list items chosen and why; initial data exploration and data quality findings; proposed approach; plan and roles; risks.
8
Model checkpoint (short report + notebook)
Data preparation and feature pipeline, baseline(s), deep learning model(s), evaluation, a first test-set submission, and the model you intend to use, with justification.
13
Prototype demonstration (15 minutes, live)
Working end-to-end prototype, including the dashboard, demonstrated on realistic ShopSphere scenarios, with early evaluation results.
16
Final report (max 25 pages + appendices)
Problem, data, model development and evaluation, agent and dashboard design and evaluation, responsible AI, results against the wish list, limitations, future work.
16
Final presentation and live demo (20 minutes + Q&A)
Presented to a panel acting as ShopSphere leadership. Every member presents.
16
Code repository and final test-set submission
Reproducible code, notebooks and README. No API keys committed.
16
Individual reflection and peer evaluation
Each member's contribution and learning; an evaluation of teammates' contributions.
9. Teamwork, constraints and rules
Each member must own at least one major component and be able to explain it in Q&A.
Use Git from Week 1 and keep a shared task board and weekly meeting log.
Use only open-source libraries and the AI models or APIs your lecturer approves. Stay within any API budget you are given.
Declare any use of generative AI tools in your report: which tools you used and what for.
Your prototype must not connect to any real messaging, email or payment system.
10. Assessment
A detailed rubric will be released separately. Broadly, you will be assessed on:
understanding of the stakeholders and the problem;
data preparation and deep learning;
agentic AI;
the dashboard and analytics;
evaluation;
responsible AI;
the prototype, report and presentation;
individual contribution.

Problem statement
ShopSphere's staff make important weekly decisions (who to re-engage, how, with which offer and through which channel) without knowing which customers are likely to purchase soon and which are drifting away. The information they need is spread across separate systems and policy documents, and pulling it together by hand is slow, inconsistent and error-prone. Managers also lack a timely view of the trends that would tell them whether these decisions are working.
How might ShopSphere use its customer, behavioural and operational data, together with AI, to predict which customers will make a purchase in the next 30 days, and help its staff turn that prediction into timely, consistent, policy-compliant and cost-effective decisions?

Raised by

CRM Manager, Finance Controller

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os

import pandas as pd

from common import OUT_DATA, OUT_OUTPUTS, OUT_REPORTS, ensure_dirs, read_budget

OBJECTIVES = {
    "incremental_revenue": "Expected incremental revenue",
    "net_value": "Expected net margin after incentive",
    "roi": "Expected net return per dollar of incentive",
    "propensity": "Purchase probability",
}


def load_scores() -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(OUT_DATA, "offer_candidate_scores.parquet"))


def budget_for(week_start, country: str) -> float:
    budget = read_budget()
    week = pd.Timestamp(week_start)
    row = budget[(budget["week_start"] == week) & (budget["country"] == country)]
    if len(row):
        return float(row["retention_budget_usd"].iloc[0])
    return float(budget["retention_budget_usd"].mean())


def seasonality_factor(week_start, country: str) -> tuple[float, str]:
    path = os.path.join(OUT_DATA, "analytics_seasonality_month.csv")
    week = pd.Timestamp(week_start)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return 1.0, "seasonality unavailable; using 1.00x"
    season = pd.read_csv(path)
    rows = season[
        (season["country"] == country) & (season["month_num"] == week.month)
    ]
    values = rows["revenue_index_vs_year_mean"].dropna()
    if values.empty:
        return 1.0, "no same-month history; using 1.00x"
    factor = float(values.median())
    factor = max(0.75, min(1.35, factor))
    return factor, f"{week.strftime('%B')} seasonal demand index {factor:.2f}x"


def build_plan(
    week_start,
    country: str,
    budget_usd: float | None = None,
    objective: str = "incremental_revenue",
    min_uplift: float = 0.0,
    min_net_value: float | None = 0.0,
    max_contacts: int | None = None,
    cooldown_days: int = 14,
    scores: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    if objective not in OBJECTIVES:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown objective {objective!r}")
    if scores is None:
        scores = load_scores()
    week = pd.Timestamp(week_start)
    df = scores[scores["cust_country"] == country].copy()
    seasonal_factor, seasonal_note = seasonality_factor(week, country)
    df["seasonal_factor"] = seasonal_factor
    df["expected_incremental_revenue"] *= seasonal_factor
    df["expected_incremental_margin"] *= seasonal_factor
    df["expected_net_value"] = df["expected_incremental_margin"] - df["offer_cost"]
    df["roi"] = (
        df["expected_net_value"] / df["offer_cost"].replace(0, pd.NA)
    )
    df["days_since_last_contact"] = (
        (week - pd.to_datetime(df["last_contact_date"])).dt.days.fillna(9999)
    )
    df = df[df["days_since_last_contact"] >= cooldown_days].copy()
    df = df[df["uplift"] >= min_uplift].copy()
    df = df[df["expected_incremental_revenue"] > 0].copy()
    if min_net_value is not None:
        df = df[df["expected_net_value"] >= min_net_value].copy()
    if objective == "roi":
        df = df[(df["expected_net_value"] > 0) & (df["offer_cost"] > 0)].copy()
    elif objective == "net_value":
        df = df[df["expected_net_value"] > 0].copy()

    if objective in ("incremental_revenue", "propensity"):
        df["priority_score"] = df["expected_incremental_revenue"]
    elif objective == "net_value":
        df["priority_score"] = df["expected_net_value"]
    else:
        df["priority_score"] = df["roi"]

    df = df.sort_values(["priority_score", "expected_net_value"], ascending=False)
    df = df.drop_duplicates("sample_ref", keep="first").copy()
    df = df.sort_values(["priority_score", "expected_net_value"], ascending=False)

    budget = float(budget_usd) if budget_usd is not None else budget_for(week, country)
    cumulative = df["offer_cost"].cumsum()
    df = df[cumulative <= budget].copy()
    if max_contacts is not None:
        df = df.head(int(max_contacts)).copy()

    df.insert(0, "week_start", week.date().isoformat())
    df.insert(1, "country", country)
    df["priority_rank"] = range(1, len(df) + 1)

    spend = float(df["offer_cost"].sum())
    inc_rev = float(df["expected_incremental_revenue"].sum())
    inc_margin = float(df["expected_incremental_margin"].sum())
    net = float(df["expected_net_value"].sum())
    summary = {
        "week_start": week.date().isoformat(),
        "country": country,
        "objective": objective,
        "objective_label": OBJECTIVES[objective],
        "budget_usd": round(budget, 2),
        "seasonal_factor": round(float(seasonal_factor), 4),
        "seasonal_note": seasonal_note,
        "planned_contacts": int(len(df)),
        "planned_spend": round(spend, 2),
        "budget_used_pct": round(spend / budget, 4) if budget else None,
        "expected_incremental_revenue": round(inc_rev, 2),
        "expected_incremental_margin": round(inc_margin, 2),
        "expected_net_value": round(net, 2),
        "expected_roi": round(net / spend, 4) if spend else None,
        "avg_uplift": round(float(df["uplift"].mean()), 5) if len(df) else None,
        "avg_purchase_probability": round(float(df["purchase_probability"].mean()), 5) if len(df) else None,
        "avg_w1_probability": round(float(df["w1_probability"].mean()), 5) if len(df) else None,
        "offer_mix": df["offer_code"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(df) else {},
        "channel_mix": df["channel"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(df) else {},
        "tier_mix": df["cust_tier"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(df) else {},
    }
    return df, summary


def main() -> None:
    ensure_dirs()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--week", default="2024-10-07")
    parser.add_argument("--country", default="US")
    parser.add_argument("--objective", default="incremental_revenue", choices=sorted(OBJECTIVES))
    parser.add_argument("--budget", type=float, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--min-uplift", type=float, default=0.0)
    parser.add_argument("--max-contacts", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--cooldown-days", type=int, default=14)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    plan, summary = build_plan(
        args.week, args.country, args.budget, args.objective, args.min_uplift,
        max_contacts=args.max_contacts, cooldown_days=args.cooldown_days,
    )
    stem = f"plan_{args.week}_{args.country}_{args.objective}"
    plan.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT_OUTPUTS, stem + ".csv"), index=False)
    with open(os.path.join(OUT_REPORTS, stem + ".json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(plan.head(10).to_string(index=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        "tier_mix": df["cust_tier"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(df) else {},
    }
    return df, summary


def main() -> None:
    ensure_dirs()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--week", default="2024-10-07")
    parser.add_argument("--country", default="US")
    parser.add_argument("--objective", default="incremental_revenue", choices=sorted(OBJECTIVES))
    parser.add_argument("--budget", type=float, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--min-uplift", type=float, default=0.0)
    parser.add_argument("--max-contacts", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--cooldown-days", type=int, default=14)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    plan, summary = build_plan(
        args.week, args.country, args.budget, args.objective, args.min_uplift,
        max_contacts=args.max_contacts, cooldown_days=args.cooldown_days,
    )
    stem = f"plan_{args.week}_{args.country}_{args.objective}"
    plan.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT_OUTPUTS, stem + ".csv"), index=False)
    with open(os.path.join(OUT_REPORTS, stem + ".json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(plan.head(10).to_string(index=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def tab_recommendations() -> None:
    st.subheader("W3 weekly retention plan")
    st.caption(
        "Plans use the offer-response model and are constrained by country budget, consent, "
        "service-recovery routing, and a contact cooldown. Costs are redemption-weighted "
        "expected incentive spend."
    )
    budget = read_budget()
    weeks = sorted(budget["week_start"].dt.date.unique())
    countries = sorted(budget["country"].unique())
    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    week = c1.selectbox("Week", weeks)
    country = c2.selectbox("Country", countries)
    objective = c3.selectbox(
        "Objective", list(planner.OBJECTIVES.keys()),
        format_func=lambda x: planner.OBJECTIVES[x],
        index=0,
    )
    budget_default = planner.budget_for(pd.Timestamp(week), country)
    budget_usd = c4.number_input("Budget cap (USD)", min_value=0.0, value=float(budget_default),
                                 step=500.0)

    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    min_uplift = c1.slider("Minimum uplift", 0.0, 0.20, 0.0, 0.005, format="%.3f")
    min_net = c2.number_input("Minimum expected net per contact", value=0.0, step=1.0)
    cooldown = c3.slider("Contact cooldown (days)", 0, 60, 14, 1)
    max_contacts = c4.number_input("Max contacts (0 = no cap)", min_value=0, value=0, step=1000)

    plan_key = (
        str(week), country, objective, round(float(budget_usd), 2),
        round(float(min_uplift), 4), round(float(min_net), 2),
        int(cooldown), int(max_contacts),
    )
    if st.button("Build plan", type="primary"):
        with st.spinner("Scoring and allocating ..."):
            plan, summary = planner.build_plan(
                week, country, budget_usd, objective, min_uplift,
                min_net_value=min_net,
                max_contacts=int(max_contacts) if max_contacts else None,
                cooldown_days=cooldown,
                scores=load_scores(),
            )
        st.session_state["plan"] = plan
        st.session_state["plan_summary"] = summary
        st.session_state["plan_key"] = plan_key

    plan = st.session_state.get("plan")
    summary = st.session_state.get("plan_summary")
    if plan is None or summary is None:
        st.info("Choose the week, country and guardrails, then build a plan.")
        return
    if st.session_state.get("plan_key") != plan_key:
        st.warning("Settings changed since this plan was built. Build a new plan to continue.")
        return
    st.caption(
        f"Plan for {summary['week_start']} · {summary['country']} · "
        f"{summary['objective_label']} · Budget {fmt_money(summary['budget_usd'])}"
    )
    seasonal_note = summary.get("seasonal_note")
    if seasonal_note:
        st.info(f"Seasonality adjustment: {seasonal_note}")
    if plan.empty:
        st.warning(
            "No recommendations meet the current guardrails. Lower the minimum net value, "
            "reduce the cooldown, or choose another objective."
        )
        return

    k1, k2, k3, k4, k5 = st.columns(5)
    k1.metric("Contacts", f"{summary['planned_contacts']:,}")
    k2.metric("Expected spend", fmt_money(summary["planned_spend"]))
    k3.metric("Incremental revenue", fmt_money(summary["expected_incremental_revenue"]))
    k4.metric("Expected net margin", fmt_money(summary["expected_net_value"]))
    k5.metric("Expected ROI", f"{summary['expected_roi']:.2f}" if summary["expected_roi"] is not None else "n/a")

    c1, c2 = st.columns(2)
    with c1:
        offer_mix = pd.DataFrame(
            {"offer": list(summary["offer_mix"].keys()),
             "contacts": list(summary["offer_mix"].values())}
        )
        st.altair_chart(
            alt.Chart(offer_mix).mark_bar().encode(
                x=alt.X("contacts:Q", title="Contacts"),
                y=alt.Y("offer:N", sort="-x", title=None),
                tooltip=["offer:N", "contacts:Q"],
            ).properties(height=220),
            width="stretch",
        )
    with c2:
        channel_mix = pd.DataFrame(
            {"channel": list(summary["channel_mix"].keys()),
             "contacts": list(summary["channel_mix"].values())}
        )
        st.altair_chart(
            alt.Chart(channel_mix).mark_bar().encode(
                x=alt.X("contacts:Q", title="Contacts"),
                y=alt.Y("channel:N", sort="-x", title=None),
                color=alt.Color("channel:N", legend=None),
                tooltip=["channel:N", "contacts:Q"],
            ).properties(height=220),
            width="stretch",
        )

    display_cols = [
        "priority_rank", "sample_ref", "cust_country", "cust_tier", "channel", "offer_code",
        "purchase_probability", "baseline_probability", "uplift", "redemption_probability",
        "offer_cost", "expected_incremental_revenue", "expected_net_value", "roi",
        "w1_probability", "priority_score",
    ]

"""Load the trained ShopSphere propensity model and score customer feature rows.

Used by the dashboard and (later) the agent so there is a single scoring API.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys

import joblib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from mlp_model import MLP  # noqa: E402

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
MODELS = os.path.join(BASE, "models")
FEAT = os.path.join(BASE, "features")
REPORTS = os.path.join(BASE, "reports")


class Scorer:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        with open(os.path.join(FEAT, "feature_metadata.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            self.meta = json.load(fh)
        with open(os.path.join(REPORTS, "metrics.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            self.metrics = json.load(fh)
        with open(os.path.join(MODELS, "mlp_meta.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            self.mlp_meta = json.load(fh)
        self.features = self.meta["feature_columns"]
        self.selected = self.metrics["selected_model"]
        self.threshold = float(self.metrics["selected_threshold"])
        self.pre = joblib.load(os.path.join(MODELS, "preprocessor.joblib"))
        self.hgb = joblib.load(os.path.join(MODELS, "hgb.joblib"))
        self.logreg = joblib.load(os.path.join(MODELS, "logreg.joblib"))
        self.mlps = []
        for seed in self.mlp_meta["seeds"]:
            m = MLP(self.mlp_meta["n_in"])
            m.load_state_dict(torch.load(os.path.join(MODELS, f"mlp_seed{seed}.pt"),
                                         map_location="cpu"))
            m.eval()
            self.mlps.append(m)

    def _transform(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
        return self.pre.transform(df[self.features]).astype("float32")

    def _mlp_probs(self, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        probs = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for m in self.mlps:
                probs.append(torch.sigmoid(m(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(X)))).numpy())
        return np.mean(probs, axis=0)

    def predict_proba(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
        X = self._transform(df)
        mlp = self._mlp_probs(X)
        hgb = self.hgb.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]
        logreg = self.logreg.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]
        table = {
            "Logistic Regression (baseline)": logreg,
            "Gradient Boosting (baseline)": hgb,
            "Deep Learning MLP (seed ensemble)": mlp,
            "Ensemble (MLP + HGB)": (mlp + hgb) / 2,
            "Ensemble (MLP + HGB + LogReg)": (mlp + hgb + logreg) / 3,
        }
        return table[self.selected]

    def predict(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
        return (self.predict_proba(df) >= self.threshold).astype(int)

Your current build has the deterministic pieces (W1 scoring, W3 planner, W9 approvals) but no agent that **chooses tools and acts**. To satisfy the brief's "agentic AI" requirement, add an LLM tool-calling layer around them.

**Minimum viable agent**
- New `solution/agent.py` + `solution/tools.py`: a system prompt, tool schemas, and a bounded ReAct loop (max ~6 steps). The agent must decide which tools to call, not follow a fixed pipeline.
- New **"Agent / Copilot"** Streamlit tab: chat box, example prompts, visible tool-call trace, final answer with tables/charts, and an **"Create approval batch"** action.
- Wrap the existing `modeling/scoring.py:Scorer` as `score_propensity(filters)` so the agent calls the actual W1 MLP+HGB ensemble, not a mock.
- Wrap `planner.build_plan(...)` as `plan_retention(week, country, budget, objective, guardrails)` so the agent uses W3.
- Wrap `approvals.create_batch(...)` as `create_approval_batch(plan, preparer)` and `record_decision(...)`. The agent prepares; a human approves.

**Tools that add the missing wish-list items**
- `explain_score(sample_ref)` → SHAP/permutation contributions from the HGB + templated reasons (W2).
- `check_policy(plan)` → consent/DNC, contact cooldown, complaint suppression, tier eligibility, budget, stock/margin (W4).
- `customer_360(sample_ref)` → orders, deliveries, tickets, recent offers, open complaints (W5).
- `ask_analytics(question)` → constrained natural-language query over whitelisted `analytics_*.csv` views; no arbitrary SQL (W7).
- `draft_message(sample_ref, offer, channel, language)` → personalised draft in `pref_language`; never sends (W8).
- `campaign_effectiveness(...)` → ROAS/CPA/DiD/offer-lift lookups (W10).

That gets you **W1–W10 coverage**, with W2/W4/W5/W7/W8 newly unlocked.

**Actions the agent can take**
- Build a plan, create a draft batch in SQLite, export a CSV, draft a message, and log every step to the existing audit log. Do not let it approve its own batch or contact customers.
- Add tool-level guardrails: allowlist tools, read-only analytics, pseudonymous `sample_ref` only, max steps, budget caps, DNC hard filter, no send/external API, and human approval before any export.

**Evidence the rubric will want**
- 12–20 scripted scenarios in `solution/scenarios/` with expected tools/answers, e.g. "Plan US 2024-10-07 under $5k and explain the top segment", "Why is sample_ref X high propensity?", "Is this plan compliant?", "Draft a German email for OFF-V15", "Did Q3 email campaigns pay back?"
- `reports/agent_evaluation.md` with task success, tool-choice accuracy, policy violations (target zero), hallucination rate, latency/cost, and human approval rate.
- Ablations: single-shot LLM vs tool-augmented agent, and agent without the W1 model, to prove the tools matter.
- Adversarial tests: asking for PII, a 20% voucher for Bronze, contacting a DNC customer, or bypassing approval — the agent must refuse/escalate.
- Log every run to `reports/agent_runs.jsonl` and show a trace in the demo.

**Implementation notes**
- Use an instructor-approved API or local model; keep keys in environment variables, never commit them, and declare the LLM in the final report.
- Provide a deterministic fallback so the prototype still works if the LLM is unavailable.
- Keep the agent segment-level and explanation-focused; never expose `customer_id`.
would having an option for the AI to send out the vouchers upon request fufil the requirement?

User asks: "would having an option for the AI to send out the vouchers upon request fulfil the requirement?" Need answer nuanced. The requirement: agentic AI component that reasons, uses tools (including trained model) and takes actions to help staff solve business problems. Also brief: "Your prototype must not connect to any real messaging, email or payment system." And W9: nothing sent without approval, recorded reason. So an "AI sends vouchers on request" could technically demonstrate action but would violate constraints if real, and would violate human-in-control W9 / responsible AI if no approval. Also "send out vouchers" is action, but not enough alone: it must reason and use trained model. A single function "send voucher" called on request is not agentic by itself — it's a tool. The agent could decide to call it, but must have policy checks and human approval, and simulate sending (write to DB/outbox, not real messaging/payment). So answer: yes in principle as an action, but only if (1) it's a simulated outbox, no real messaging/payment, (2) gated by human approval, consent, DNC, tier eligibility, budget, cooldown, audit, (3) agent reasoning/selection uses model and tools, not just direct command, (4) "upon request" should mean staff request, not customer or autonomous send. Need distinguish "AI sends" vs "AI prepares send request".

Maybe they ask if this alone fulfils the agentic AI component. Answer: no, not by itself. It can be one action tool, but requirement needs reasoning + model + tools + actions. A button that sends vouchers is automation, not agency. Also W9 says nothing sent without approval; real sending is prohibited. So implement "stage for approval" / "simulated dispatch to outbox with approval" and include agent rationale.

Could mention: If they want, add `dispatch_offer(batch_id, channel)` that writes to a `dispatch_outbox` table with status "Queued/Sent (simulated)" only after approval and policy check; audit log. Demonstrate in demo with a "Send" button after approval. That is credible. Avoid actually emailing.

Also mention eval: show refusal when DNC, Bronze+20%, no approval. Good.

Need concise answer. Maybe bullets. Use code references? Not needed. The question is conceptual. Keep under ~15 lines.

Not by itself. A "send voucher" button is automation, not an agent. The requirement is that the AI **reasons, chooses tools (including your trained model), and takes an action** — so sending would be one **action tool**, not the whole component.

Also, sending vouchers "upon request" conflicts with the brief and your W9 design unless it's constrained:

- **No real messaging/email/payment** — the brief forbids it. Simulate it: write to a `dispatch_outbox` table with status `Queued`/`Sent (simulated)`.
- **Human approval first** — W9 says nothing is sent without approval and a recorded reason. The agent can prepare a batch and request approval, but cannot self-approve or auto-send.
- **Policy checks before dispatch** — consent, DNC, tier eligibility (no 20% voucher for Bronze), open complaints, cooldown, weekly budget, stock/margin.
- **Agent must decide** — e.g. the request is "win back dormant Gold customers in DE under €3k"; the agent scores customers, picks offers/channels, checks policy, builds the batch, then requests dispatch approval. A direct "send OFF-V20 to everyone" command should be refused or escalated.
- **Audit everything** — agent trace, approver, reason, offer/channel, counts, and simulated dispatch result.

So the strongest version is `dispatch_offers(batch_id)` as a guarded tool: **approval + policy check + simulated outbox + audit log**. That, combined with `score_propensity`, `plan_retention`, `explain_score`, `check_policy`, and `draft_message`, would satisfy the agentic requirement and demonstrate action safely.

The user: "for this project we need to have a use for AI outside of what a predictive analysis tool can do, proving use for AI". They seem to be saying the agentic AI component needs to justify AI beyond predictive analytics. They ask implicitly: what use? We need respond with how to prove the AI (LLM/agent) adds value beyond prediction. Should explain the distinction: predictive model outputs scores; AI agent does reasoning, tool orchestration, natural-language interaction, explanation, policy reasoning, message drafting, multi-source synthesis, planning, evaluation/reflection, handling ambiguity/edge cases. Need show evidence it's not just deterministic code. Maybe propose a concrete "agentic" use case and an evaluation to prove it.

Need interpret "proving use for AI" — probably for report rubric: "use of AI outside of what a predictive analysis tool can do". They need to demonstrate AI's unique value. We should propose specific capabilities and an experiment proving it. Key argument: the prediction is necessary but insufficient; staff need to turn predictions into decisions. LLM agent provides:
1. Natural-language task delegation and multi-step planning (W7).
2. Tool selection/orchestration across heterogeneous sources (W5, W4).
3. Reasoning over unstructured policy docs and support ticket messages (RAG), which predictive model can't do.
4. Explanation generation grounded in model evidence (W2).
5. Writing personalized multilingual outreach (W8).
6. Adaptive exception handling/reflection: detects insufficient data, adjusts budget/cooldown, asks clarification.
7. Human-in-loop approval and audit.

To "prove" AI use:

## 1. Scope for now: W1, W3, W6, W9, W10

The agent should sit on top of these five, using the trained model as a tool rather than replacing it. W4 policy checks and W5 customer context can exist as internal guardrails, but they don't need to be headline deliverables yet.

## 2. Seasonality in W1 (the important change)

Your instinct is right: seasonality should not live only in W6. The current model predicts a **fixed October 2024 window** from a hard-coded `CUTOFF = 2024-09-30`. For a rolling "next 30 days from the as-of date" score, I'd change W1 to:

- Make `as_of` a parameter, not a constant.
- Build features **only from data on or before `as_of`**.
- Add **target-window seasonality**: the month(s) the next 30 days fall in, holiday proximity (Singles' Day, Black Friday, Christmas), country-specific seasonal demand index, prior same-month activity, and dormant × holiday-affinity interactions.
- Train on multiple historical as-of snapshots (e.g. monthly cutoffs) with labels `purchase in (as_of, as_of+30d]`.
- Validate with **time-based splits and a 30-day embargo**, because overlapping 30-day labels leak if snapshots are adjacent.
- Keep the official Oct 2024 train/test model for the required submission, and add a separate **rolling/as-of mode** for the prototype. Otherwise you risk breaking the graded deliverable.

This makes W1 answer "how likely is this customer to buy in the *specific* next 30 days?" rather than "how likely is a customer in this tier/category to buy in October?" Seasonality also affects:

- **W3:** projected incremental revenue and offer choice vary by window; budget pacing can be seasonal.
- **W6:** seasonal indices and comparisons become first-class views.
- **W9:** recorded reasons cite the seasonal factor and whether the customer is a seasonal buyer.
- **W10:** compare campaign outcomes against a seasonal baseline/DiD so holiday demand isn't credited to the campaign.

## 3. Revised wish definitions (proposer → issue → success)

**W1 — Predict purchases within 30 days** *(CRM Manager)*
- Issue: manual lists are stale; vouchers go to people who would have bought anyway; tier mistakes happen.
- Revised: estimate each customer's purchase probability for the next 30 days from the as-of date, using only data available then, with seasonality; expose the score and top drivers; refresh quickly.

**W3 — Weekly re-engagement recommendations within country budgets** *(CRM Manager + Finance Controller)*
- Issue: list-building takes 1.5 days and is out of date; same 10% voucher for most people; spending isn't targeted.
- Revised: use W1, customer profile/preferences, eligible offers and country budgets to produce a fast, prioritised who/offer/channel list, ranked by expected incremental value; avoid likely buyers; choose voucher type from customer data; keep within budget and policy.

**W6 — Business analytics dashboard** *(Head of Marketing + Operations Manager + Leadership)*
- Issue: monthly slide decks, no at-a-glance channel/region/season comparison; carrier problems suspected but not proven.
- Revised: self-serve sales, traffic, campaign, delivery and customer-activity trends by country and over time, plus a carrier scorecard that shows late/lost/returned rates and cost to customers.

**W9 — Human approval and recorded reasons** *(CRM Manager)*
- Issue: automated actions without oversight; no audit trail.
- Revised: no simulated outreach until a human approves; record the recommendation reason, reviewer, decision and timestamp; maintain an immutable audit trail; simulated dispatch only.

**W10 — Evaluate campaign effectiveness** *(Finance Controller)*
- Issue: spend rises but nobody can say what worked.
- Revised: track spend, purchases, redemptions and attributed revenue; where comparison data exists, estimate incremental impact against a seasonal baseline or control group, so Finance can judge whether the money made a difference.

## 4. Two data sets

Yes — separate **training/backtest** from **live/operational** data:

- **Training corpus:** immutable as-of snapshots, each with a version, cutoff date, schema version, checksum, row counts, quality report and labels. Used to train and backtest the rolling W1 model.
- **Live snapshot:** refreshed weekly, used by W3/W9/W10 and the app. The model is pinned to a specific snapshot so results are reproducible.
- Keep the original data pack immutable. For the prototype, simulate live updates from the pack or clearly labelled synthetic rows. Add drift and freshness monitors.

Strictly there are three layers: raw/immutable → curated snapshots → live inference. The standard train/validation/test split still applies inside the training corpus.

## 5. Agentic data-cleaning idea

This is a genuine "AI outside prediction" use, but keep it bounded:

- Agent tools: profile table, validate schema/types, detect duplicates/missing/invalid values, check referential integrity, compare distributions, propose cleaning rules, apply them to **staging only**, write a quality report, request approval, publish a new snapshot.
- The agent reasons about what is wrong and **proposes** a cleaning plan; deterministic functions actually transform data. Destructive actions require human approval.
- Never mutate raw data, never silently delete rows, version every snapshot, and log every change.
- Evaluate with before/after data-quality metrics, model performance on cleaned vs raw, correction error rate, reproducibility and time saved.

This also supports W3's freshness problem: a scheduled cleaning/validation agent can produce the next trusted snapshot and trigger rescoring.

## 6. Implementation order when you're ready

1. Refactor `CUTOFF` to `as_of`; add snapshot builder and rolling labels.
2. Add target-window seasonality features; retrain and backtest W1.
3. Update W3 planner to use the rolling score and window seasonality.
4. Extend W6 with seasonal/carrier views.
5. Add W9 simulated dispatch + reasons/audit.
6. Add W10 seasonal-adjusted effectiveness.
7. Only then build the live snapshot + cleaning agent.

204:     f = f.join(shares(t, "customer_id", "payment_method", PAYMENTS, "txn_pay_"))
205:     f = f.join(shares(t, "customer_id", "shipping_speed", SHIP_SPEEDS, "txn_ship_"))
206: 
207:     # Seasonality: historical October / holiday buying behaviour. The target window is
208:     # October 2024, so a customer's prior-October activity is a direct seasonal signal;
209:     # Nov-Dec affinity captures seasonal shoppers who are otherwise dormant.
210:     t["_month"] = t["d"].dt.month
211:     t["_is_oct"] = t["_month"].eq(10).astype(int)
212:     t["_is_holiday"] = t["_month"].isin([11, 12]).astype(int)
213:     t["_is_q4"] = t["_month"].isin([10, 11, 12]).astype(int)
214:     t["_year_month"] = t["d"].dt.to_period("M")
215:     seas = t.groupby("customer_id").agg(
216:         txn_oct_n=("_is_oct", "sum"),

218:         txn_q4_n=("_is_q4", "sum"),
219:     )
220:     seas["txn_oct_share"] = seas["txn_oct_n"] / f["txn_n"]
221:     seas["txn_holiday_share"] = seas["txn_holiday_n"] / f["txn_n"]
222:     seas["txn_q4_share"] = seas["txn_q4_n"] / f["txn_n"]
223:     seas["txn_oct_active"] = (seas["txn_oct_n"] > 0).astype(int)
224:     seas["txn_holiday_active"] = (seas["txn_holiday_n"] > 0).astype(int)
225:     monthly = t.groupby(["customer_id", "_year_month"]).size().rename("n").reset_index()
226:     mg = monthly.groupby("customer_id")["n"]
227:     seas["txn_monthly_mean"] = mg.mean()
228:     seas["txn_monthly_max"] = mg.max()
229:     seas["txn_monthly_std"] = mg.std()

232:     )
233:     seas["txn_month_cv"] = (
234:         seas["txn_monthly_std"] / seas["txn_monthly_mean"].replace(0, np.nan)
235:     )
236:     last_oct = t[t["_is_oct"] == 1].groupby("customer_id")["d"].max()
237:     seas["txn_days_since_last_oct"] = (CUTOFF - last_oct).dt.days
238:     f = f.join(seas)
239:     f["txn_dormant_holiday_affinity"] = (
240:         (f["txn_days_since_last"] > 180).astype(int) * f["txn_holiday_share"]

245: def item_features(txn: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
246:     items = read("transaction_items.csv")
247:     products = read("products.csv", usecols=["product_id", "category", "margin_pct"])
248:     items = items.merge(products, on="product_id", how="left")
249:     items["line_value"] = items["quantity"] * items["unit_price"]
250:     items = items.merge(txn[["transaction_id", "customer_id", "d"]], on="transaction_id", how="left")
251:     items = items.dropna(subset=["customer_id"])
252:     items["customer_id"] = items["customer_id"].astype("int64")
253: 
254:     g = items.groupby("customer_id")
255:     f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)
256:     f["item_lines"] = g.size()
257:     f["item_qty"] = g["quantity"].sum()
258:     f["item_list_value"] = g["line_value"].sum()
259:     f["item_weighted_margin"] = (
260:         items.assign(_w=items["line_value"] * items["margin_pct"]).groupby("customer_id")["_w"].sum()
261:         / g["line_value"].sum().replace(0, np.nan)
262:     )
263:     low_margin = items.assign(
264:         _lm=np.where(items["margin_pct"] < 0.25, items["line_value"], 0.0)
265:     ).groupby("customer_id")["_lm"].sum()
266:     f["item_low_margin_share"] = low_margin / g["line_value"].sum().replace(0, np.nan)
267: 
268:     cat = items.groupby(["customer_id", "category"])["line_value"].sum().unstack(fill_value=0.0)
269:     cat = cat.div(cat.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan), axis=0)
270:     cat.columns = [f"item_cat_{c}" for c in cat.columns]
271:     f = f.join(cat)
272:     return f

275: def delivery_features(txn: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
276:     d = read("deliveries.csv")
277:     d = d.merge(txn[["transaction_id", "customer_id", "d"]].rename(columns={"d": "txn_d"}),
278:                 on="transaction_id", how="left")
279:     d = d.dropna(subset=["customer_id"])

281:     d["_late"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "Delivered Late").astype(int)
282:     d["_lost"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "Lost").astype(int)
283:     d["_returned"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "Returned").astype(int)
284:     d["_transit"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "In Transit").astype(int)

286:     g = d.groupby("customer_id")

291:     f["del_lost_rate"] = g["_lost"].mean()
292:     f["del_returned_rate"] = g["_returned"].mean()
293:     f["del_transit_rate"] = g["_transit"].mean()
294:     f["del_delay_mean"] = g["delay_days"].mean()
295:     f["del_delay_max"] = g["delay_days"].max()
296:     f["del_delay_sum"] = g["delay_days"].sum()
297:     f["del_last_status_late"] = (
298:         d.sort_values(["customer_id", "txn_d"]).groupby("customer_id")["_late"].last()
299:     )
300:     return f

303: def support_features() -> pd.DataFrame:
304:     s = read("support_tickets.csv")
305:     s["d"] = pd.to_datetime(s["created_date"])
306:     s = s[s["d"] <= CUTOFF].copy()
307:     s["_open"] = (s["status"] == "Open").astype(int)
308:     s["_high"] = (s["priority"] == "High").astype(int)
309:     s["_low_csat"] = (s["csat_score"] <= 2).astype(int)

311:     g = s.groupby("customer_id")
312:     f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)

314:     f["sup_open_n"] = g["_open"].sum()
315:     f["sup_high_n"] = g["_high"].sum()
316:     f["sup_low_csat_n"] = g["_low_csat"].sum()
317:     f["sup_days_since_last"] = (CUTOFF - g["d"].max()).dt.days
318:     f["sup_csat_mean"] = g["csat_score"].mean()
319:     f["sup_fr_mean"] = g["first_response_hours"].mean()
320:     f["sup_fr_max"] = g["first_response_hours"].max()
321:     f["sup_res_mean"] = g["resolution_hours"].mean()

323:     f["sup_n_90d"] = s.assign(_m=s["d"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=90)).groupby("customer_id")["_m"].sum()
324: 
325:     f = f.join(counts(s, "customer_id", "category", TICKET_CATS, "sup_cat_"))

334: def retention_features() -> pd.DataFrame:

347:     f["ret_redeem_rate"] = g["_redeemed"].mean()
348:     f["ret_purch14_rate"] = g["_p14"].mean()
349:     f["ret_no_offer_n"] = g["_no_offer"].sum()
350:     f["ret_v20_n"] = g["_v20"].sum()
351:     f["ret_days_since_last"] = (CUTOFF - g["d"].max()).dt.days
352:     f = f.join(shares(r, "customer_id", "channel", RET_CHANNELS, "ret_ch_"))
353:     return f
354: 
355: 
356: def region_marketing_features() -> pd.DataFrame:
357:     camp = read("marketing_campaigns.csv")
358:     perf = read("campaign_daily_performance.csv")
359:     agg = perf.groupby("campaign_id").agg(
360:         spend=("spend", "sum"), revenue=("attributed_revenue", "sum"),
361:         orders=("attributed_orders", "sum"), clicks=("clicks", "sum"),
362:         impressions=("impressions", "sum"),
363:     ).reset_index()
364:     camp = camp.merge(agg, on="campaign_id", how="left")
365:     reg = camp.groupby("region_target").agg(
366:         reg_spend=("spend", "sum"), reg_revenue=("revenue", "sum"),

368:         reg_impressions=("impressions", "sum"), reg_campaigns=("campaign_id", "count"),
369:         reg_budget_mean=("campaign_budget", "mean"),

372:     reg["reg_ctr"] = reg["reg_clicks"] / reg["reg_impressions"].replace(0, np.nan)
373: 
374:     perf["date"] = pd.to_datetime(perf["date"])
375:     recent = perf[perf["date"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=90)]
376:     recent = recent.merge(camp[["campaign_id", "region_target"]], on="campaign_id", how="left")
377:     reg_recent = recent.groupby("region_target")["spend"].sum().rename("reg_spend_90d")
378:     reg = reg.join(reg_recent)

display.text:
"""
ShopSphere - customer-level feature engineering for the 30-day purchase target.

Reads the cleaned tables in ../shopsphere_data and builds one row per customer
using only information up to the snapshot cutoff (2024-09-30), so the October
target is never leaked.

Outputs (../modeling/features):
    train_features.pkl   customer_id + features + target
    test_features.pkl    customer_id + features
    feature_metadata.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA = os.path.join(BASE, "..", "shopsphere_data")
OUT = os.path.join(BASE, "features")
CUTOFF = pd.Timestamp("2024-09-30")

TRAFFIC = ["organic", "direct", "ads", "email", "social"]
DEVICE = ["mobile", "desktop", "tablet"]
CAMPAIGN_TYPES = ["Email", "Search", "Display", "Social", "Affiliate"]
PAYMENTS = ["credit_card", "debit_card", "paypal", "crypto"]
SHIP_SPEEDS = ["standard", "express", "overnight"]
DELIVERY_STATUS = ["Delivered", "Delivered Late", "Lost", "Returned", "In Transit"]
TICKET_CATS = [
    "Late delivery", "Damaged or wrong item", "Product question", "Refund status",
    "Lost parcel", "Payment issue", "Account access", "Promo code not working", "Cancel order",
]
RET_CHANNELS = ["email", "app_push", "sms"]


def read(name: str, **kw) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA, name), low_memory=False, **kw)


def days_since(dates: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    return (CUTOFF - pd.to_datetime(dates)).dt.days


def to01(s: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """Map booleans / TRUE-FALSE / Y-N encodings to 1/0 (NaN stays NaN)."""
    if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s):
        return s.astype("int64")
    low = s.astype("string").str.strip().str.lower()
    return low.map({"true": 1, "false": 0, "y": 1, "n": 0, "yes": 1, "no": 0,
                    "1": 1, "0": 0, "t": 1, "f": 0})


def shares(df: pd.DataFrame, id_col: str, cat_col: str, categories: list[str], prefix: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    tmp = df[[id_col, cat_col]].dropna()
    tab = tmp.groupby([id_col, cat_col]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
    tab = tab.reindex(columns=categories, fill_value=0)
    out = tab.div(tab.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan), axis=0)
    out.columns = [f"{prefix}{c}" for c in out.columns]
    return out


def counts(df: pd.DataFrame, id_col: str, cat_col: str, categories: list[str], prefix: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    tmp = df[[id_col, cat_col]].dropna()
    tab = tmp.groupby([id_col, cat_col]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
    tab = tab.reindex(columns=categories, fill_value=0)
    tab.columns = [f"{prefix}{c}" for c in tab.columns]
    return tab


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def customer_base() -> pd.DataFrame:
    c = read("customers.csv")
    c["tenure_days"] = days_since(c["signup_date"])
    c["email_open_rate_missing"] = c["email_open_rate"].isna().astype(int)
    c["has_referral"] = c["referral_code"].notna().astype(int)
    c["tier_ord"] = c["customer_tier"].map({"Bronze": 0, "Silver": 1, "Gold": 2, "Platinum": 3})
    c = c.rename(columns={
        "age": "cust_age", "country_code_clean": "cust_country", "region": "cust_region",
        "loyalty_score": "cust_loyalty", "email_open_rate": "cust_email_open",
        "discount_usage_rate": "cust_discount_rate", "avg_review_score": "cust_review",
        "customer_tier": "cust_tier", "credit_limit": "cust_credit_limit",
        "email_open_rate_missing": "cust_email_open_missing",
    })
    keep = ["customer_id", "cust_age", "cust_country", "cust_region", "tenure_days",
            "cust_loyalty", "cust_email_open", "cust_email_open_missing",
            "cust_discount_rate", "cust_review", "has_referral", "cust_tier", "tier_ord",
            "cust_credit_limit"]
    base = c[keep].copy()

    geo = read("geo_data.csv").rename(columns={
        "geo_ip_region": "cust_region", "average_income": "geo_income",
        "urban_ratio": "geo_urban", "internet_penetration": "geo_internet",
        "region_tier": "geo_tier",
    })
    base = base.merge(geo, on="cust_region", how="left")

    pref = read("customer_preferences.csv")
    pref["pref_days_since_update"] = days_since(pref["last_updated"])
    for col in ["email_opt_in_clean", "sms_opt_in_clean", "do_not_contact_clean"]:
        pref[col] = to01(pref[col])
    pref = pref.rename(columns={
        "email_opt_in_clean": "pref_email_opt", "sms_opt_in_clean": "pref_sms_opt",
        "preferred_channel": "pref_channel", "preferred_language": "pref_language",
        "do_not_contact_clean": "pref_dnc",
    })
    base = base.merge(
        pref[["customer_id", "pref_email_opt", "pref_sms_opt", "pref_channel",
              "pref_language", "pref_dnc", "pref_days_since_update"]],
        on="customer_id", how="left",
    )
    return base


def session_features() -> pd.DataFrame:
    s = read("shopsphere_sessions_cleaned.csv")
    s["ts"] = pd.to_datetime(s["session_timestamp"])
    s = s[s["ts"] <= CUTOFF].copy()
    s["_bounce"] = to01(s["bounce_clean"])
    s["_camp"] = (s["campaign_status"] == "Has Campaign").astype(int)

    g = s.groupby("customer_id")
    f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)
    f["sess_n"] = g.size()
    f["sess_days_since_last"] = (CUTOFF - g["ts"].max()).dt.days
    f["sess_tenure_days"] = (CUTOFF - g["ts"].min()).dt.days
    for d in (30, 90, 180, 365):
        f[f"sess_n_{d}d"] = s.assign(_m=s["ts"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=d)).groupby("customer_id")["_m"].sum()
    for col, out in [("session_duration", "dur"), ("pages_viewed", "pages"),
                     ("cart_additions", "cart")]:
        f[f"sess_{out}_mean"] = g[col].mean()
        f[f"sess_{out}_max"] = g[col].max()
        f[f"sess_{out}_sum"] = g[col].sum()
    f["sess_dur_std"] = g["session_duration"].std()
    f["sess_bounce_rate"] = g["_bounce"].mean()
    f["sess_campaign_rate"] = g["_camp"].mean()
    f["sess_campaign_n"] = g["_camp"].sum()

    f = f.join(shares(s, "customer_id", "traffic_source_clean", TRAFFIC, "sess_src_"))
    f = f.join(shares(s, "customer_id", "device_type_clean", DEVICE, "sess_dev_"))

    # Seasonality: how much of this customer's browsing happens in the target month
    # (October) and in the Nov-Dec holiday peak, across the multi-year history.
    s["_month"] = s["ts"].dt.month
    s["_is_oct"] = s["_month"].eq(10).astype(int)
    s["_is_holiday"] = s["_month"].isin([11, 12]).astype(int)
    s["_is_q4"] = s["_month"].isin([10, 11, 12]).astype(int)
    s["_year_month"] = s["ts"].dt.to_period("M")
    seas = s.groupby("customer_id").agg(
        sess_oct_n=("_is_oct", "sum"),
        sess_holiday_n=("_is_holiday", "sum"),
        sess_q4_n=("_is_q4", "sum"),
    )
    seas["sess_oct_share"] = seas["sess_oct_n"] / f["sess_n"]
    seas["sess_holiday_share"] = seas["sess_holiday_n"] / f["sess_n"]
    seas["sess_q4_share"] = seas["sess_q4_n"] / f["sess_n"]
    monthly = s.groupby(["customer_id", "_year_month"]).size().rename("n").reset_index()
    mg = monthly.groupby("customer_id")["n"]
    seas["sess_monthly_mean"] = mg.mean()
    seas["sess_monthly_max"] = mg.max()
    seas["sess_seasonal_index"] = (
        seas["sess_monthly_max"] / seas["sess_monthly_mean"].replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    f = f.join(seas)

    camp = read("marketing_campaigns.csv", usecols=["campaign_id", "campaign_type"])
    sm = s[["customer_id", "campaign_id"]].dropna(subset=["campaign_id"]).copy()
    sm["campaign_id"] = sm["campaign_id"].astype("int64")
    sm = sm.merge(camp, on="campaign_id", how="left")
    f = f.join(shares(sm, "customer_id", "campaign_type", CAMPAIGN_TYPES, "sess_camptype_"))
    return f


def transaction_features() -> pd.DataFrame:
    t = read("transactions.csv")
    t["d"] = pd.to_datetime(t["transaction_timestamp"])
    t = t[t["d"] <= CUTOFF].sort_values(["customer_id", "d"]).copy()
    t["_disc"] = to01(t["discount_applied_clean"])
    t["_high"] = to01(t["high_value_flag_clean"])

    g = t.groupby("customer_id")
    f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)
    f["txn_n"] = g.size()
    f["txn_days_since_last"] = (CUTOFF - g["d"].max()).dt.days
    f["txn_tenure_days"] = (CUTOFF - g["d"].min()).dt.days
    for d in (30, 90, 180, 365):
        f[f"txn_n_{d}d"] = t.assign(_m=t["d"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=d)).groupby("customer_id")["_m"].sum()
        f[f"txn_spend_{d}d"] = t.assign(_v=np.where(t["d"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=d), t["order_value"], 0.0)).groupby("customer_id")["_v"].sum()
    for col, out in [("order_value", "value"), ("items_count", "items")]:
        f[f"txn_{out}_mean"] = g[col].mean()
        f[f"txn_{out}_max"] = g[col].max()
        f[f"txn_{out}_sum"] = g[col].sum()
    f["txn_value_std"] = g["order_value"].std()
    f["txn_value_median"] = g["order_value"].median()
    f["txn_discount_rate"] = g["_disc"].mean()
    f["txn_high_value_rate"] = g["_high"].mean()
    f["txn_last_value"] = g["order_value"].last()
    f["txn_last_items"] = g["items_count"].last()
    f["txn_spend_per_day"] = f["txn_value_sum"] / f["txn_tenure_days"].replace(0, np.nan)

    f = f.join(shares(t, "customer_id", "payment_method", PAYMENTS, "txn_pay_"))
    f = f.join(shares(t, "customer_id", "shipping_speed", SHIP_SPEEDS, "txn_ship_"))

    # Seasonality: historical October / holiday buying behaviour. The target window is
    # October 2024, so a customer's prior-October activity is a direct seasonal signal;
    # Nov-Dec affinity captures seasonal shoppers who are otherwise dormant.
    t["_month"] = t["d"].dt.month
    t["_is_oct"] = t["_month"].eq(10).astype(int)
    t["_is_holiday"] = t["_month"].isin([11, 12]).astype(int)
    t["_is_q4"] = t["_month"].isin([10, 11, 12]).astype(int)
    t["_year_month"] = t["d"].dt.to_period("M")
    seas = t.groupby("customer_id").agg(
        txn_oct_n=("_is_oct", "sum"),
        txn_holiday_n=("_is_holiday", "sum"),
        txn_q4_n=("_is_q4", "sum"),
    )
    seas["txn_oct_share"] = seas["txn_oct_n"] / f["txn_n"]
    seas["txn_holiday_share"] = seas["txn_holiday_n"] / f["txn_n"]
    seas["txn_q4_share"] = seas["txn_q4_n"] / f["txn_n"]
    seas["txn_oct_active"] = (seas["txn_oct_n"] > 0).astype(int)
    seas["txn_holiday_active"] = (seas["txn_holiday_n"] > 0).astype(int)
    monthly = t.groupby(["customer_id", "_year_month"]).size().rename("n").reset_index()
    mg = monthly.groupby("customer_id")["n"]
    seas["txn_monthly_mean"] = mg.mean()
    seas["txn_monthly_max"] = mg.max()
    seas["txn_monthly_std"] = mg.std()
    seas["txn_seasonal_index"] = (
        seas["txn_monthly_max"] / seas["txn_monthly_mean"].replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    seas["txn_month_cv"] = (
        seas["txn_monthly_std"] / seas["txn_monthly_mean"].replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    last_oct = t[t["_is_oct"] == 1].groupby("customer_id")["d"].max()
    seas["txn_days_since_last_oct"] = (CUTOFF - last_oct).dt.days
    f = f.join(seas)
    f["txn_dormant_holiday_affinity"] = (
        (f["txn_days_since_last"] > 180).astype(int) * f["txn_holiday_share"]
    )
    return f, t


def item_features(txn: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    items = read("transaction_items.csv")
    products = read("products.csv", usecols=["product_id", "category", "margin_pct"])
    items = items.merge(products, on="product_id", how="left")
    items["line_value"] = items["quantity"] * items["unit_price"]
    items = items.merge(txn[["transaction_id", "customer_id", "d"]], on="transaction_id", how="left")
    items = items.dropna(subset=["customer_id"])
    items["customer_id"] = items["customer_id"].astype("int64")

    g = items.groupby("customer_id")
    f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)
    f["item_lines"] = g.size()
    f["item_qty"] = g["quantity"].sum()
    f["item_list_value"] = g["line_value"].sum()
    f["item_weighted_margin"] = (
        items.assign(_w=items["line_value"] * items["margin_pct"]).groupby("customer_id")["_w"].sum()
        / g["line_value"].sum().replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    low_margin = items.assign(
        _lm=np.where(items["margin_pct"] < 0.25, items["line_value"], 0.0)
    ).groupby("customer_id")["_lm"].sum()
    f["item_low_margin_share"] = low_margin / g["line_value"].sum().replace(0, np.nan)

    cat = items.groupby(["customer_id", "category"])["line_value"].sum().unstack(fill_value=0.0)
    cat = cat.div(cat.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan), axis=0)
    cat.columns = [f"item_cat_{c}" for c in cat.columns]
    f = f.join(cat)
    return f


def delivery_features(txn: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    d = read("deliveries.csv")
    d = d.merge(txn[["transaction_id", "customer_id", "d"]].rename(columns={"d": "txn_d"}),
                on="transaction_id", how="left")
    d = d.dropna(subset=["customer_id"])
    d["customer_id"] = d["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    d["_late"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "Delivered Late").astype(int)
    d["_lost"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "Lost").astype(int)
    d["_returned"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "Returned").astype(int)
    d["_transit"] = (d["delivery_status"] == "In Transit").astype(int)

    g = d.groupby("customer_id")
    f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)
    f["del_n"] = g.size()
    f["del_carriers"] = g["carrier"].nunique()
    f["del_late_rate"] = g["_late"].mean()
    f["del_lost_rate"] = g["_lost"].mean()
    f["del_returned_rate"] = g["_returned"].mean()
    f["del_transit_rate"] = g["_transit"].mean()
    f["del_delay_mean"] = g["delay_days"].mean()
    f["del_delay_max"] = g["delay_days"].max()
    f["del_delay_sum"] = g["delay_days"].sum()
    f["del_last_status_late"] = (
        d.sort_values(["customer_id", "txn_d"]).groupby("customer_id")["_late"].last()
    )
    return f


def support_features() -> pd.DataFrame:
    s = read("support_tickets.csv")
    s["d"] = pd.to_datetime(s["created_date"])
    s = s[s["d"] <= CUTOFF].copy()
    s["_open"] = (s["status"] == "Open").astype(int)
    s["_high"] = (s["priority"] == "High").astype(int)
    s["_low_csat"] = (s["csat_score"] <= 2).astype(int)

    g = s.groupby("customer_id")
    f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)
    f["sup_n"] = g.size()
    f["sup_open_n"] = g["_open"].sum()
    f["sup_high_n"] = g["_high"].sum()
    f["sup_low_csat_n"] = g["_low_csat"].sum()
    f["sup_days_since_last"] = (CUTOFF - g["d"].max()).dt.days
    f["sup_csat_mean"] = g["csat_score"].mean()
    f["sup_fr_mean"] = g["first_response_hours"].mean()
    f["sup_fr_max"] = g["first_response_hours"].max()
    f["sup_res_mean"] = g["resolution_hours"].mean()
    f["sup_res_max"] = g["resolution_hours"].max()
    f["sup_n_90d"] = s.assign(_m=s["d"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=90)).groupby("customer_id")["_m"].sum()

    f = f.join(counts(s, "customer_id", "category", TICKET_CATS, "sup_cat_"))
    f = f.join(shares(s, "customer_id", "channel_clean", ["Live chat", "Email", "WhatsApp", "Phone"], "sup_ch_"))

    complaint_cats = ["Late delivery", "Damaged or wrong item", "Lost parcel", "Refund status"]
    recent = s[(s["d"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=90)) & (s["category"].isin(complaint_cats))]
    f["sup_recent_complaint"] = f.index.isin(recent["customer_id"]).astype(int)
    return f


def retention_features() -> pd.DataFrame:
    r = read("retention_contact_history.csv")
    r["d"] = pd.to_datetime(r["contact_date"])
    r = r[r["d"] <= CUTOFF].copy()
    r["_redeemed"] = to01(r["redeemed_clean"])
    r["_p14"] = to01(r["purchased_within_14d_clean"])
    r["_no_offer"] = (r["offer_code"] == "OFF-NONE").astype(int)
    r["_v20"] = (r["offer_code"] == "OFF-V20").astype(int)

    g = r.groupby("customer_id")
    f = pd.DataFrame(index=g.size().index)
    f["ret_n"] = g.size()
    f["ret_redeemed_n"] = g["_redeemed"].sum()
    f["ret_redeem_rate"] = g["_redeemed"].mean()
    f["ret_purch14_rate"] = g["_p14"].mean()
    f["ret_no_offer_n"] = g["_no_offer"].sum()
    f["ret_v20_n"] = g["_v20"].sum()
    f["ret_days_since_last"] = (CUTOFF - g["d"].max()).dt.days
    f = f.join(shares(r, "customer_id", "channel", RET_CHANNELS, "ret_ch_"))
    return f


def region_marketing_features() -> pd.DataFrame:
    camp = read("marketing_campaigns.csv")
    perf = read("campaign_daily_performance.csv")
    agg = perf.groupby("campaign_id").agg(
        spend=("spend", "sum"), revenue=("attributed_revenue", "sum"),
        orders=("attributed_orders", "sum"), clicks=("clicks", "sum"),
        impressions=("impressions", "sum"),
    ).reset_index()
    camp = camp.merge(agg, on="campaign_id", how="left")
    reg = camp.groupby("region_target").agg(
        reg_spend=("spend", "sum"), reg_revenue=("revenue", "sum"),
        reg_orders=("orders", "sum"), reg_clicks=("clicks", "sum"),
        reg_impressions=("impressions", "sum"), reg_campaigns=("campaign_id", "count"),
        reg_budget_mean=("campaign_budget", "mean"),
    )
    reg["reg_roas"] = reg["reg_revenue"] / reg["reg_spend"].replace(0, np.nan)
    reg["reg_ctr"] = reg["reg_clicks"] / reg["reg_impressions"].replace(0, np.nan)

    perf["date"] = pd.to_datetime(perf["date"])
    recent = perf[perf["date"] >= CUTOFF - pd.Timedelta(days=90)]
    recent = recent.merge(camp[["campaign_id", "region_target"]], on="campaign_id", how="left")
    reg_recent = recent.groupby("region_target")["spend"].sum().rename("reg_spend_90d")
    reg = reg.join(reg_recent)
    reg.index.name = "cust_region"
    return reg


def country_budget() -> pd.Series:
    rb = read("retention_budget_2024Q4.csv")
    return rb.groupby("country")["retention_budget_usd"].mean().rename("country_avg_weekly_budget")


def main() -> None:
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    print("Building customer base ...")
    base = customer_base()

    print("Sessions ...")
    sess = session_features()
    print("Transactions ...")
    txn, txn_raw = transaction_features()
    print("Items ...")
    items = item_features(txn_raw)
    print("Deliveries ...")
    deliv = delivery_features(txn_raw)
    print("Support ...")
    sup = support_features()
    print("Retention contacts ...")
    ret = retention_features()
    print("Region marketing ...")
    reg = region_marketing_features()
    print("Country budget ...")
    budget = country_budget()

    feats = base.copy()
    for block in (sess, txn, items, deliv, sup, ret):
        feats = feats.merge(block, left_on="customer_id", right_index=True, how="left")
    feats = feats.merge(reg, left_on="cust_region", right_index=True, how="left")
    feats = feats.merge(budget, left_on="cust_country", right_index=True, how="left")

    count_prefixes = ("sess_n", "txn_n", "item_lines", "item_qty", "del_n", "sup_n", "ret_n",
                      "ret_redeemed_n", "ret_no_offer_n", "ret_v20_n")
    for col in feats.columns:
        if col.startswith(count_prefixes):
            feats[col] = feats[col].fillna(0)

    train_ids = read("train.csv")
    test_ids = read("test.csv")
    train = train_ids.merge(feats, on="customer_id", how="left")
    test = test_ids.merge(feats, on="customer_id", how="left")
    assert len(train) == len(train_ids) and len(test) == len(test_ids)

    feature_cols = [c for c in feats.columns if c != "customer_id"]
    cat_cols = [c for c in ["cust_country", "cust_region", "cust_tier", "geo_tier",
                            "pref_channel", "pref_language"] if c in feature_cols]
    num_cols = [c for c in feature_cols if c not in cat_cols]

    train.to_pickle(os.path.join(OUT, "train_features.pkl"))
    test.to_pickle(os.path.join(OUT, "test_features.pkl"))
    meta = {
        "cutoff": str(CUTOFF.date()),
        "n_features": len(feature_cols),
        "categorical": cat_cols,
        "numeric": num_cols,
        "train_rows": int(len(train)),
        "test_rows": int(len(test)),
        "positive_rate": float(train["target"].mean()),
        "feature_columns": feature_cols,
    }
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "feature_metadata.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(meta, fh, indent=2)

    print(f"Train {train.shape}  Test {test.shape}  features={len(feature_cols)}")
    print(f"Categorical: {cat_cols}")
    print(f"Numeric: {len(num_cols)}")
    print("Saved features to", OUT)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

]

    "country_avg_weekly_budget",
]
SESSION_FEATURES = [
    "sess_n", "sess_days_since_last", "sess_tenure_days", "sess_n_30d", "sess_n_90d",
    "sess_n_180d", "sess_n_365d", "sess_dur_mean", "sess_dur_max", "sess_dur_sum",
    "sess_pages_mean", "sess_pages_max", "sess_pages_sum", "sess_cart_mean",
    "sess_cart_max", "sess_cart_sum", "sess_dur_std", "sess_bounce_rate",
    "sess_campaign_rate", "sess_campaign_n", "sess_src_organic", "sess_src_direct",
    "sess_src_ads", "sess_src_email", "sess_src_social", "sess_dev_mobile",
    "sess_dev_desktop", "sess_dev_tablet", "sess_camptype_Email",

]
TXN_FEATURES = [
    "txn_n", "txn_days_since_last", "txn_tenure_days", "txn_n_30d", "txn_spend_30d",
    "txn_n_90d", "txn_spend_90d", "txn_n_180d", "txn_spend_180d", "txn_n_365d",

OFFER_FEATURES = [

]
VALUE_FEATURES = ["expected_order_value", "margin"]

CUSTOMER_FEATURES = BASE_FEATURES + SESSION_FEATURES + TXN_FEATURES + ITEM_FEATURES + \
    DELIVERY_FEATURES + SUPPORT_FEATURES + VALUE_FEATURES

MODEL_FEATURES = CUSTOMER_FEATURES + OFFER_FEATURES

CATEGORICAL_FEATURES = [
    "cust_country", "cust_region", "cust_tier", "geo_tier", "pref_channel",
    "pref_language", "offer_code", "channel", "offer_type",
]


def ensure_dirs() -> None:
    for path in (OUT_DATA, OUT_MODELS, OUT_REPORTS, OUT_OUTPUTS):
        os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)


def read_csv(name: str, **kwargs) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, name), low_memory=False, **kwargs)


def to01(s: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s):
        return s.astype("int64")
    low = s.astype("string").str.strip().str.lower()
    return low.map({
        "true": 1, "false": 0, "y": 1, "n": 0, "yes": 1, "no": 0,
        "1": 1, "0": 0, "t": 1, "f": 0,
    })


def safe_div(a, b):
    return np.divide(a, b, out=np.full_like(np.asarray(a, dtype=float), np.nan),
                     where=np.asarray(b, dtype=float) != 0)


def sample_ref(ids: Iterable) -> pd.Series:
    def one(value) -> str:
        return "S" + hashlib.sha1(str(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]

    return pd.Series([one(v) for v in ids], dtype="string")


def offer_catalogue() -> pd.DataFrame:
    offers = read_csv("offer_catalogue.csv")
    offers["requires_promotable"] = to01(offers["requires_promotable_items_clean"]).fillna(0).astype(int)
    offers["counts_monthly"] = pd.to_numeric(
        offers["counts_toward_monthly_limit"], errors="coerce"
    ).fillna(0).astype(int)
    offers["value"] = pd.to_numeric(offers["value"], errors="coerce").fillna(0.0)
    offers["tier_list"] = offers["eligible_tiers"].fillna("All").astype(str).str.split(",")
    return offers[[
        "offer_code", "description", "offer_type", "value", "eligible_tiers",
        "tier_list", "requires_promotable", "counts_monthly",
    ]].copy()


def tiers_for_offer(row) -> list[str]:
    tiers = row["tier_list"]
    if isinstance(tiers, str):
        tiers = [tiers]
    if any(str(t).strip().lower() == "all" for t in tiers):
        return TIERS
    return [str(t).strip() for t in tiers]


def offer_cost_series(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    aov = pd.to_numeric(df.get("expected_order_value"), errors="coerce").fillna(AOV_FALLBACK)
    value = pd.to_numeric(df.get("offer_value"), errors="coerce").fillna(0.0)
    kind = df.get("offer_type", pd.Series("No offer", index=df.index)).astype(str)
    cost = np.select(
        [kind.eq("Shipping"), kind.eq("Voucher"), kind.eq("Points"), kind.eq("Credit")],
        [6.0, value * aov, 3.0, 10.0], default=0.0,
    )
    return pd.Series(cost, index=df.index, dtype=float)


def read_budget() -> pd.DataFrame:
    budget = read_csv("retention_budget_2024Q4.csv")
    budget["week_start"] = pd.to_datetime(budget["week_start"])
    budget["country"] = budget["country"].astype(str)
    return budget


def region_country_map() -> pd.Series:
    customers = read_csv("customers.csv", usecols=["region", "country_code_clean"])
    out = customers.dropna().groupby("region")["country_code_clean"] \
        .agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0])
    out.index.name = "cust_region"
    return out


def shares(df: pd.DataFrame, id_col: str, cat_col: str, categories: list[str], prefix: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    tmp = df[[id_col, cat_col]].dropna()
    tab = tmp.groupby([id_col, cat_col]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
    tab = tab.reindex(columns=categories, fill_value=0)
    out = tab.div(tab.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan), axis=0)
    out.columns = [f"{prefix}{c}" for c in out.columns]
    return out


def counts(df: pd.DataFrame, id_col: str, cat_col: str, categories: list[str], prefix: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    tmp = df[[id_col, cat_col]].dropna()
    tab = tmp.groupby([id_col, cat_col]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
    tab = tab.reindex(columns=categories, fill_value=0)
    tab.columns = [f"{prefix}{c}" for c in tab.columns]
    return tab

173:     for col, out in [("order_value", "value"), ("items_count", "items")]:
174:         f[f"txn_{out}_mean"] = g[col].mean()

209:         / g["line_value"].sum().replace(0, np.nan)
